extracted.intended_audience: students of philosophy, political theorists, and lawmakers interested in designing an ideal state's education and leadership
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for the education, selection, and moral/institutional formation of guardians/philosopher-kings in an ideal state, including curriculum, stages, personal qualities, and institutional arrangements. Emphasises mathematical and dialectical training as preparation for apprehending the Good and ruling rightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic as essential philosophical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic must be taught not as a commercial art but as a discipline that compels the soul to reason about abstract number and to use pure intelligence to attain pure truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach arithmetic until students 'see the nature of numbers with the mind only.' It should be pursued in the spirit of a philosopher (not a shopkeeper), for its elevating effect and for preparing the mind to pass from becoming to truth. Arithmetic also improves general quickness of apprehension, even in otherwise dull students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry oriented to eternal being (not mere practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometry should be taught in the aspect that relates to knowledge of eternal being rather than merely for practical, everyday operations (squaring, measuring, applying).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise the parts of geometry that draw the soul toward the idea of the Good; avoid restricting geometry to mundane applications. Follow a proper intellectual order (plane geometry before solids in themselves, then solids in revolution). State patronage may be required to develop advanced solid geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy as philosophical pattern, not empirical fixation
rubrics_metrics.description: Astronomy should be used as a pattern to lead the soul away from mere sensible particulars toward reasoned apprehension of true motions (absolute swiftness/slowess), rather than as an empirical study of visible celestial particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the starry heavens as patterns; employ problems and reasoned analysis rather than relying on sight or investigating the exact material proportions of celestial bodies. Treat astronomy as a preparation for higher knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony/music studied for mathematical/natural harmonies
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of musical harmony should aim at understanding the natural, numerical principles underlying harmony, not only the audible consonances that musicians debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a purely empirical or technical approach that measures the smallest audible intervals; seek the number-based reasons why certain ratios are harmonious and their relation to beauty and the good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical sciences as handmaids to dialectic (understanding vs science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical disciplines (arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, harmony) are useful preparatory studies that approximate awareness of being but remain dependent on hypotheses and so are not ultimate science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these sciences to train the mind and as instruments for dialectic, but subject their hypotheses to examination; they should be transcended by dialectic which seeks first principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic as the highest discipline (coping-stone of sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic alone reaches the first principles and does away with hypotheses, enabling the mind to perceive absolute being and the idea of the Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign dialectic only to those who have been discipled in the previous sciences; dialectic is the final stage that lifts the 'eye of the soul' to absolute truth and must be the culmination of education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for advanced study: natural gifts required
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective rulers must possess natural faculties that facilitate arduous intellectual training: keenness, quickness of acquisition, good memory, and a love of labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer those with ready powers of acquisition and stamina for intellectual toil; these qualities are more decisive than bodily prowess for bearing the severity of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and character qualifications (virtue completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must be sound in virtue (temperance, courage, magnificence, truthfulness), with no 'lame' or partial virtues; partial or defective virtue produces rulers who err.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish true sons of philosophy from 'bastards'—ensure candidates are not half-industrious, nor tolerant of involuntary falsehood, nor shamefully ignorant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of eristic/lawlessness through staged timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Early or mistimed exposure to dialectic can produce lawlessness and eristic habits (contradicting for amusement) leading to social disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce dialectic cautiously and in proper stages so youth do not prematurely adopt contradicting-for-amusement patterns; ensure moderation and maturity before deep dialectical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compulsive early intellectual education
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge should not be acquired under compulsion; early education should be made a form of amusement so that learning takes root willingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While compulsory physical training harms less, compulsion in intellectual learning produces no durable hold on the mind. Use engaging, playful methods in childhood to discover natural bent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and staging of education (age-based progression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education must follow an ordered sequence: early elementary studies in childhood, gymnastics, selection tests, then higher unification of disciplines and eventual dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children should begin calculation/geometry etc. in childhood, not by force. After initial gymnastics and elementary studies, at age ~20 the best are promoted to higher studies; later stages include dialectic testing and eventual consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit durations and practical alternation of study and life
rubrics_metrics.description: The curriculum prescribes time periods for study and for returning to public/military life to gain experience and test firmness under temptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested schedule: elementary gymnastics (2–3 years), higher mathematical/introductory studies (unspecified early years), five years of dedicated dialectical study, then fifteen years of practical service ('sent down into the den') to gain experience, with final elevation around age fifty for consummating philosophical study and public duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial by practical experience to test character
rubrics_metrics.description: After advanced study, students must be sent into ordinary life and public/military service to determine whether they remain steadfast when tempted and whether philosophic habits endure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use practical offices and military duties as tests of whether candidates will 'stand firm or flinch' when drawn by desires; performance during these years contributes to final selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final qualification: ability to apprehend and defend the idea of the Good
rubrics_metrics.description: A true ruler must be capable of abstracting, defining, and defending the idea of the Good, meeting objections by appeal to absolute truth rather than opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require the capacity to run the gauntlet of objections, to reason without appealing to opinion, and to maintain unflinching argument through all steps; only then can one rightly order the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical robustness and endurance for prolonged discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be sound in body as well as mind—unwearied, lovers of labour—since the mental toil is severe and requires endurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors those who can endure both bodily exercise and long intellectual discipline; the mind 'more often faints from severity of study' so stamina is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: State patronage to cultivate advanced, neglected sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The State should actively patronise difficult branches of learning (e.g., solid geometry) that private life neglects, in order to secure directors and discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without government support such fields languish; public encouragement will attract disciples, continuous search, and progress into 'light'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal life and property for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should live communally with no private possessions or ordinary property; they receive maintenance from the citizens and devote themselves to protecting the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up common houses, shared families (wives and children in common), and limit guardians' property to maintenance-only to prevent private interest from corrupting public duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender equality in education where natures permit
rubrics_metrics.description: Women who have the appropriate natures should share the same education as men and be eligible for the same roles in the guardian class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume the described education applies to men only; provide equal training to women 'as far as their natures can go.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-patterns to avoid in candidates' temperament and habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid recruiting those who are half-industrious (lovers of bodily exercise but hating intellectual labour), those patient in involuntary falsehood, or those who practice contradiction for amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware pupils who imitate eristic argument for sport, or who are conceited and inattentive to directors; ensure vocation and earnestness in philosophical pursuit.
